summary:
Cult of Skaro is a Dalek artifact-aggro deck whose attack trigger picks a random mode. This review re-verifies all eleven items of the deck's rules attestation.

Rules points:
- Copies (Strionic Resonator, Scientist Supreme) repeat the rolled mode; Roaming Throne gives a fresh roll.
- The Master, Multiplied keeps myriad tokens.

No list errors.

interactions.title: The random mode is chosen as the trigger goes on the stack
interactions.ruling:
Cult of Skaro's attack trigger is modal, with the mode chosen at random. Modes are chosen when a triggered ability is put on the stack, so everyone knows the result before anyone responds. It triggers on being *declared* as an attacker, not on entering attacking.
- **Thay:** +1/+1 counter on each artifact creature you control.
- **Caan:** draw two.
- **Sec:** a 3/3 menace Dalek token.
- **Jast:** each opponent loses 4.
interactions.short: Attack trigger: one of four modes at random, fixed as it goes on the stack.

oracle.quote: Whenever Cult of Skaro attacks, choose one at random —

source.item: Cult of Skaro attack trigger and random mode timing

interactions.title: Copies keep the mode; extra triggers re-roll
interactions.ruling:
- **Strionic Resonator ({2}, {T}) and Scientist Supreme (pay 2 life, once per turn, your turn, artifact source):** these *copy* the trigger, and a copy keeps the already chosen mode.
- **Roaming Throne (naming Dalek):** makes Cult trigger an additional time, a separate trigger that rolls its own random mode.

Use copies when you like the roll; Throne gives more chances.
interactions.short: Resonator/Scientist copies repeat the rolled mode; Roaming Throne gives a fresh roll.

oracle.quote: Pay 2 life: Copy target activated or triggered ability you control from an artifact source. You may choose new targets for the copy. Activate only during your turn and only once each turn.

source.item: Cult of Skaro + Scientist Supreme of A.I.M.

interactions.title: Helm of the Host, Spark Double, Sakashima, Auton Soldier copies
interactions.ruling:
These copies of Cult each have the attack trigger:
- **Helm of the Host:** a hasty nonlegendary token copy at each beginning of combat on your turn, including extra combats.
- **Spark Double and Auton Soldier:** nonlegendary copies.
- **Sakashima:** turns off the legend rule for your permanents.

Each copy declared as an attacker rolls its own mode. Myriad tokens (from Auton Soldier) enter attacking and weren't declared, so their copied Cult trigger doesn't fire that combat.

oracle.quote: At the beginning of combat on your turn, create a token that's a copy of equipped creature, except the token isn't legendary. That token gains haste.

source.item: Cult of Skaro + Helm of the Host
Auton Soldier copy of Cult and myriad tokens

interactions.title: The Master, Multiplied keeps myriad tokens
interactions.ruling: The Master stops your triggered abilities from sacrificing or exiling your creature tokens, so myriad's 'exile at end of combat' trigger does nothing. Dalek Squadron, Auton Soldier and Cybermen Squadron's myriad tokens stay. It also turns off the legend rule for creature tokens. Those tokens weren't declared attackers the combat they appeared, but they can attack in later combats and trigger their own abilities (myriad, a copied Cult trigger).

oracle.quote: Triggered abilities you control can't cause you to sacrifice or exile creature tokens you control.

rulings.quote: Notably, the part of myriad that makes you exile the creature tokens at end of combat is a triggered ability. This means that the ability will trigger, but you won't exile the tokens when it resolves.

interactions.title: Sword of Feast and Famine + Aggravated Assault
interactions.ruling: When the equipped creature connects, Sword untaps all your lands. In the next main phase, Aggravated Assault ({3}{R}{R}, sorcery speed) untaps your creatures and adds another combat and main phase. Repeat for unlimited combats, with each Cult attack rolling again. You need lands producing {3}{R}{R} and a creature that connects.
interactions.short: Spellbook infinite combats: Sword untaps lands, Assault adds combats.

oracle.quote: {3}{R}{R}: Untap all creatures you control. After this main phase, there is an additional combat phase followed by an additional main phase. Activate only as a sorcery.

source.item: Aggravated Assault + Sword of Feast and Famine

interactions.title: Full Throttle and Great Train Heist extra combats
interactions.ruling:
- **Full Throttle:** cast in a main phase, it adds two combats (no main phase between them) and untaps the creatures that attacked at the start of each combat that turn.
- **Great Train Heist:** the first spree mode during your combat untaps your creatures and adds one more combat right after, with no main phase.

Each new attack with Cult rolls again.

rulings.quote: There is no main phase between the two additional combat phases.
Notably, Great Train Heist’s first mode doesn’t give you any additional main phases.

source.item: Great Train Heist additional combat mode

interactions.title: Arena of Glory haste; Plaza of Heroes protection
interactions.ruling: Arena of Glory's exert mana gives haste to a creature spell it's spent on, so a fresh Cult can attack that turn. Plaza of Heroes can exile itself to give a legendary creature hexproof and indestructible until end of turn.

oracle.quote: If any of that mana is spent on a creature spell, it gains haste until end of turn.

interactions.title: Exterminate! replicates by tapping Daleks
interactions.ruling: Exterminate!'s replicate cost is tapping an untapped Dalek. Cult, Davros's tokens, Dalek Squadron and the Sec tokens all count. Each payment adds a copy (destroy a creature, its controller loses 3). Daleks that attacked are tapped unless untapped again, so cast it before combat or after an untap.

oracle.quote: Replicate—Tap an untapped Dalek you control.

interactions.title: Biotransference and Their Name Is Death or Delete
interactions.ruling: Biotransference makes your creatures artifacts, so Their Name Is Death (nonartifact creatures) and Delete (nonartifact creatures) spare them. Cult and the Daleks are artifacts already. Thay's counters go on every artifact creature you control, so with Biotransference that's every creature.

oracle.quote: Creatures you control are artifacts in addition to their other types.

interactions.title: Commander tax and artifact recursion
interactions.ruling: Cult costs {1}{U}{B}{R}, then 6, then 8. It's an artifact, so if you leave it in the graveyard Academy Ruins can put it on top of your library.

oracle.quote: {1}{U}, {T}: Put target artifact card from your graveyard on top of your library.
